newsitem.title: USA: Dole attacked as hypocritical on pardons issue.
newsitem.headline: Dole attacked as hypocritical on pardons issue.

text.p: Republican challenger Bob Dole, who has demanded President Bill Clinton disavow pardons for his Whitewater business partners, successfully persuaded President George Bush to pardon a key Cabinet official in the Iran-Contra affair, according to a new book.

Lawrence Walsh, the independent prosecutor who investigated the Reagan administration's efforts to sell arms to Iran and funnel the proceeds to rebels in Nicaragua, said on Tuesday Dole was "the foremost advocate" of a pardon for Defence Secretary Caspar Weinberger.

In his book, "Firewall: The Iran-Contra Conspiracy and Cover-up," Walsh notes that when Dole failed to derail legal proceedings against Weinberger he lobbied Bush to pardon the secretary in advance of trial.
"Sen. Dole's demand that President Clinton forego future pardons connected with Whitewater gives the voters a remarkable view of Dole's hypocrisy ..." Walsh said in a statement.
Two chapters of the book, which will be published by W. W. Norton and Co. next spring, were released by Walsh "in the interest of full disclosure during the current presidential campaign."
Walsh said Dole's public concern about what Clinton might do sharply contrasted with his actions during the Iran-Contra investigation.

He charged Dole with exploiting Clinton's connection with long-ago business transactions that ended before he became president while Dole, himself, "had urged pardons for crimes of constitutional dimension committed in office by a Reagan Cabinet officer."
Weinberger was indicted in June 1992 on felony charges stemming from his alleged withholding of personal notebooks from investigators of the arms scandal.
But in December 1992, Bush pardoned him and five other Reagan administration officials involved in the affair.

"It was never intended that the pardon power of the president be used to block a trial of an indicted person," said Walsh. "Pardons have been traditionally granted as an act of mercy after conviction and usually after service of sentence, not to prevent the public exposure of embarrassing facts in the course of a public trial."

Dole, trailing in polls with three weeks to go before the Nov. 5 election, has launched an attack on the ethics of the Clinton administration, including a demand that the president pledge not to grant pardons in connection with Whitewater.
"He had better make it very clear -- no pardons, no pardons for anybody he did business with who may be in jail," Dole said on Monday.
